title: BcMath\Number
summary: PHP 8.4 added the immutable BcMath\Number value object for arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic, with object-returning arithmetic methods and operator support alongside the existing procedural BCMath APIs.
new_code_policy: When the project feature ceiling is PHP 8.4 or newer, BcMath\Number is available as an immutable object-oriented representation for arbitrary-precision decimal values. Keep decimal inputs as strings and pass scale explicitly when the result scale matters. The procedural bc* APIs remain valid and are not deprecated, so choosing BcMath\Number is an API-design decision rather than a required migration.
existing_code_policy: Do not mechanically rewrite working procedural BCMath code. Once the project floor reaches PHP 8.4, consider BcMath\Number where immutable value-object semantics improve the surrounding design, while preserving decimal-string input boundaries and explicit scale decisions. In strict-types code, do not replace a decimal string with a float constructor argument: the measured PHP 8.4 runtime rejects that argument with TypeError.
guideline: Use BcMath\Number on PHP 8.4+ when immutable object-oriented arbitrary-precision decimal values fit the design; preserve decimal strings and explicit scale, and keep procedural BCMath code when it is already the clearer interface.
details: PHP 8.4 UPGRADING section 7 (BCMath) adds the immutable BcMath\Number class, whose arithmetic methods return objects and which supports arithmetic operators. This is a feature rule, so applicability is governed by the project feature floor: the class must not be emitted for a project that still supports PHP 8.2 or 8.3. The issue #19 runtime probe on PHP 8.4.25 measured new BcMath\Number('1.20')->add('0.035', 3) as a new object with decimal value 1.235 and scale 3 while the original remains 1.20 with scale 2; procedural bcadd() produced the same decimal string. The same probe measured a float constructor argument under strict types raising TypeError. None of this deprecates or invalidates the procedural BCMath API.
notes: Procedural BCMath functions remain supported; this feature rule does not mark them deprecated and does not require an automatic rewrite to BcMath\Number.

Pinned analyzer probe from issue #19 (PHP_CodeSniffer 3.13.6 + PHPCompatibility 10.0.0-alpha2): PHPCompatibility.Classes.NewClasses.bcmath_numberFound produced 1 / 1 / 0 / 0 findings with the ceiling held at 8.5 and floors set to 8.2 / 8.3 / 8.4 / 8.5, establishing introduced_in: 8.4.

Runtime evidence from issue #19 on PHP 8.4.25: new BcMath\Number('1.20')->add('0.035', 3) produced value 1.235 at scale 3, the original remained 1.20 at scale 2, and procedural bcadd() produced the same decimal string; a float constructor argument raised TypeError under strict types.

The same issue #19 probe produced no PHPCompatibility findings for static Dom\HTMLDocument::createFromString or Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString calls. This rule therefore adds no DOM mapping and makes no claim of exhaustive DOM coverage.
